title: Matched CalCOFI oxygen boundaries narrowed by 30.6 m without a resolved full density-width change in 1984-2020
abstract: We test whether CalCOFI oxygen-transition narrowing in depth also occurs in potential density. A uniform density shift preserves boundary density separation. In 220 matched station-quarter groups at 56 stations, the 4-to-2 mL/L depth separation fell by 30.65 m between 1984-2002 and 2003-2020. Its potential-density separation changed by -0.02756 kg/m3, with conditional 95 percent limits of -0.05929 to 0.00672. All planned full-width oxygen sensitivity intervals include zero. An exact descriptive split puts 25.54 m of the depth change in the effective depth-to-density scale term; this is not a causal attribution. AOU 75-to-175 umol/kg density width also has no resolved change in the broad periods. The 125-to-175 interval narrows, but its modern-period test is uncertain. A secondary 1984-1996 to 2009-2020 comparison gives a full AOU width change of -0.06402 (-0.11600 to -0.00685). Thus depth narrowing alone cannot reject a density shift, while local AOU evidence against an exact shift depends on the periods. This test does not reject the outcrop mechanism or show a fixed profile shape. It reuses existing observations; missing profiles, finite bottle gaps, source methods and long ocean variation limit inference. Code, raw-input reconstruction, source hashes, figures, aggregate results and numerical audits are included. External record-level data stay outside the package.

Earlier boundary density test; both new oxygen boundaries also reach lighter water.
